title: Can Carpet Be Installed Over Existing Carpet, Hardwood or Concrete?
meta: Carpet over old carpet is a no, over hardwood is possible with care, over concrete is routine after a moisture test. Wills Flooring explains each for Seattle.
keywords: can you install carpet over carpet, carpet over hardwood floors, carpet over concrete basement, installing carpet on concrete slab, carpet over existing carpet padding, tack strip on hardwood

blocks.lead: Carpet should never go over existing carpet, it can go over hardwood if you accept tack strip holes, and it goes over concrete all the time once the slab passes a moisture test.
blocks.detail: The rule is simple: new carpet needs a firm, clean, dry base and something to stretch against. Old carpet fails the first test, hardwood raises a should-you question, and concrete just needs the right pad and fasteners.

blocks.html: This one comes up in three very different Seattle houses. A Beacon Hill landlord wants to lay new carpet over the tired carpet in a rental to skip a tear-out. A Wallingford buyer just found oak under the bedroom carpet and wants soft floors anyway. And a Capitol Hill condo owner or a West Seattle homeowner with a daylight basement has a bare concrete slab and a plan. Each case has its own honest answer.

blocks.text: Carpet over existing carpet: why every installer says no

items.title: Pad on pad means no stretch
items.text: Stretch-in carpet is pulled tight over a dense pad and hooked onto tack strip at the walls. Old carpet is soft and moves under the new one, so the new carpet never holds tension. Within months it ripples, and the wrinkles walk across the room every time someone drags a chair.

items.title: You seal in 15 years of what is in there
items.text: Old carpet holds dust, pet dander, spills and, in a lot of Seattle rentals, old cat urine that reached the pad. Covering it does not remove the smell; it traps it under a layer that now cannot be cleaned. Allergies get worse, not better.

items.title: Doors and transitions stop working
items.text: Two layers of carpet and pad add well over an inch. Doors drag, the strip at the tile threshold becomes a trip edge, and closet doors on tracks stop closing. In a 1920s Ballard house with original doors, planing them is not something you want to do.

items.title: No warranty covers it
items.text: Every carpet manufacturer requires new carpet over an approved pad on a clean subfloor. Install over old carpet and the material warranty is void on day one, and the installer will not warranty the stretch either. The tear-out you saved comes back as a replacement.

blocks.text: Carpet over hardwood: it works, but ask yourself why

blocks.html: Mechanically, hardwood is a great base for carpet. It is flat, firm and dry, and tack strip nails into it easily. The problem is the other direction. Half the hardwood floors we refinish in Seattle came out from under carpet, and the tack strip holes along every wall are the tell. If the wood under your carpet is oak or old-growth fir in decent shape, refinishing is often the better long-term move. If you still want carpet, here is how to do it without ruining the wood for the next owner.

head: Concern
What happens
How to protect the hardwood
rows: Rows of small nail holes about 1/2 in from the wall on every side
Use short-pin strip and accept the holes; they sit under the baseboard shadow line and sand out at a future refinish.
Hundreds of staple holes across the field of the floor
Ask for a pad that is taped at the seams and tacked only at the perimeter, not stapled across the room.
Steam cleaning pushes water through the pad into the wood, which can cup fir
Dry-clean methods only, and a pad with a moisture-resistant film if the room will be shampooed.
Carpet over wood is quiet, which is why Seattle condos with wood subfloors and downstairs neighbors often want it
This is a genuine plus. Many buildings require a sound-rated pad over wood; check the HOA rules.
blocks.note: If the hardwood is thin, cupped or already sanded several times, carpet over it is a reasonable way to keep the house comfortable without a full replacement.

a.title: It makes sense
items: Bedrooms in a house where the hardwood has been sanded to its limit
A condo where the HOA requires soft flooring or a sound-rated pad
A nursery or a home for an older parent where warmth and fall protection matter
You plan to keep the wood for a future owner and accept the tack strip holes

b.title: Keep the wood bare
items: The floor is oak or fir with enough thickness left to sand
The room is a main floor, hallway or living space in a resale-sensitive Seattle neighborhood
Someone in the house has allergies
You want the option of area rugs and a warmer look than wall-to-wall

blocks.text: Carpet over concrete: routine, with three conditions

items.text: Seattle slabs in daylight basements and on-grade condo floors are cool and often damp. A calcium chloride or relative humidity test tells us whether the slab can take carpet and what pad it needs.
items.note: A slab that fails is not a dead end; it changes the pad and sometimes the carpet type.

items.text: Over concrete we use a pad with a moisture barrier film or a synthetic fiber pad that does not absorb water. A standard rebond pad soaks up slab moisture and starts to smell within a couple of winters.

Wood-floor tack strip has short pins. Concrete strip has hardened masonry nails, or it is glued with construction adhesive where the slab is too hard or has heat tubes. Either way the carpet stretches exactly the same.

A concrete floor in a West Seattle or Magnolia basement sits near ground temperature all year. A thicker, denser pad makes a noticeable difference in comfort and is the main reason people choose carpet down there instead of vinyl plank.

blocks.text: When concrete is the wrong base for carpet

items.html: The slab has flooded or wicks water in winter. Seattle basements built into a hillside with no working drain are a recurring theme. Fix the water first; no pad survives a wet slab.
Efflorescence or dark patches that never dry. White mineral bloom on the slab means water is moving through it. That room wants a sealed slab and vinyl plank, not carpet.

Radiant heat in the slab. Carpet over heated concrete works, but only with a thin, low insulation pad, and you cannot nail tack strip into a slab with tubes in it. We glue the strip and confirm the tube layout first.

blocks.text: What to have ready before we come out

items: Pull back a corner of the old carpet in a closet and look. Wood, plywood, particleboard or concrete each change the plan.
In a condo, get the building's flooring rules. Many Seattle buildings specify a sound rating for pad and set quiet hours and elevator reservations for the install.
Tell us about smells or past leaks. We would rather see a stain on the subfloor than seal it under new carpet.
Know your priority: warmth, quiet, allergies or resale. It decides carpet versus refinish over hardwood and pad thickness over concrete.

faq.q: Can you lay new carpet on top of old carpet to save money?
faq.a: No. New carpet needs a firm base to stretch against, and old carpet is soft and moves. The new carpet ripples within months, doors stop clearing, trapped odors stay trapped, and both the material warranty and the installer's warranty are void. Tear-out is a small part of the job.

faq.q: Does carpet ruin hardwood floors underneath?
faq.a: Not the carpet itself. The damage is the tack strip nail holes around the perimeter and pad staples in the field, both of which sand out at a future refinish. Water from steam cleaning is the real risk, especially on old-growth fir in older Seattle homes. Keep cleaning dry and the wood will be fine.

faq.q: Should I carpet over the hardwood or refinish it?
faq.a: If the wood is oak or fir with sanding thickness left and the room is a living area, refinishing usually adds more value in Seattle. Carpet over hardwood makes sense in bedrooms, condos with sound requirements, and homes where warmth matters most.

faq.q: Do you need a special pad for carpet over concrete?
faq.a: Yes. Over a slab we use a pad with a moisture barrier film or a non-absorbent synthetic fiber pad. Standard rebond pad wicks moisture from cool Seattle slabs and develops a musty smell. The slab is moisture tested first so the pad choice matches the actual conditions in your basement or condo.

faq.q: How is tack strip attached to concrete?
faq.a: Concrete tack strip uses hardened masonry nails driven into the slab, or it is glued with construction adhesive when the slab is very hard, crumbly, or has radiant tubing in it. Once the strip is down, the carpet is power stretched onto it exactly the way it would be on a wood subfloor.

faq.q: Can carpet go over a concrete basement floor that has had water before?
faq.a: Only after the water problem is solved and the slab tests dry. A basement that seeps every winter will ruin any pad and grow mold under the carpet. Fix the drainage or sealing first, retest, and if the slab still reads damp, vinyl plank is the safer floor for that room.
